newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS CAN LIFT TITLE AGAINST PARMA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS CAN LIFT TITLE AGAINST PARMA.

text.p: Champions Cup finalists Juventus will pick up their 24th Italian league title on Sunday if they beat second placed Parma in Turin.
Following Thursday's league programme, leaders Juventus look assured of the title since they take a six point lead into their clash with Parma, with only two games remaining after that.
Juventus increased their lead over Parma by two points on Thursday when beating Piacenza 4-1 on a night when Parma were held to a 1-1 home draw by AC Milan.
Even if Parma beat Juventus on Sunday, the leaders would still have the cushion of a three point advantage before facing Atalanta away and Lazio at home in their last two games.

Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti had no difficulty in conceding that his side's championship challenge had faltered irrevocably against Milan on Thursday, saying afterwards: "Well, we still have our dreams. Our objective is still the runners-up spot, a placing that matters a lot to us.
"And we can now go to Turin, proud that we're able to take the field on a level footing with the strongest side of the moment."
Juventus coach Marcello Lippi was understandably reluctant to claim that his side had already won the title.
"We've won the title if we win on Sunday, that's what the arithmetic says. But until then, let's wait," he said.
"We've always had a very high opinion of Parma and that view hasn't changed a jot."
Less cautious was Juventus midfielder, Frenchman Zinedine Zidane who said afterwards: "At this stage, the title contest is all over and on Sunday we'll write the final word.
"We're in good shape and the match with Parma will be a good game, without real pressure, given our six point lead."
Juventus will be strengthened by the return of experienced defender Ciro Ferrara, suspended against Piacenza, but may still be without injured Uruguyan defender Paolo Montero.

In attack, coach Lippi has an embarrassment of riches and can choose from the quartet of Croat Alen Boksic, Christian Vieri, Nicola Amoruso and Alessandro Del Piero, all of whom played at least one half against Piacenza.
Parma too will be at close to full strength with only injured Croat midfielder Mario Stanic missing from Ancelotti's ideal first team.

As usual the Parma attack will be led by Enrico Chiesa, scorer of their goal against Milan, and Argentine Hernan Crespo, scorer of what looked an 86th minute winner against Milan that was controversially disallowed by referee Robert Boggi.
